comments.content: This third-party action is referenced by a mutable branch. In the `pull_request_target` run it executes with `pull-requests: write` and access to `LLM_API_KEY`, so a branch update or compromise in the action repository could execute arbitrary code with those privileges. Pin the action to a reviewed full commit SHA (and update it deliberately).

The workflow can accumulate redundant reviews when multiple pushes or label events arrive close together. Add a concurrency group keyed by repository and pull request (with `cancel-in-progress: true`) so superseded runs do not consume runners or duplicate review comments.
comments.suggestion_code:
name: Code review

concurrency:
  group: themis-${{ github.repository }}-pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

comments.content: There is no job timeout, so a hung action or LLM request can consume an Ubuntu runner indefinitely. Set an appropriate `timeout-minutes` value on this job.

The `in_array` arguments are reversed: its first argument is the needle and its second argument must be the array haystack. With any non-empty `fruit`, `$fruit` is passed as the haystack, causing a `TypeError` on PHP 8+ (and preventing the stock/out-of-stock response). Pass `$fruit` first and `$fruits` second.

This message contradicts the condition: `1 > $code` is true when the code is less than 1, so requests with values below 1 are reported as greater than 1. Swap this text (and the corresponding `else` text) or adjust the condition.
The `else` branch is reached when `$code` is greater than or equal to 1, but this newly changed message says it is less than 1. This produces an incorrect response for the normal code path.
comments.suggestion_code: echo 'Code is greater than or equal to 1';

comments.content: The API key is supplied as a workflow expression in an action `with` input. Action inputs can be exposed to the action implementation or appear in diagnostic/process data more readily than environment variables; avoid passing credentials as inputs when possible, and use the action's documented environment-variable mechanism (or otherwise ensure it does not log the input).
